title: What does LoanSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of LoanSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, LoanSet establishes a loan agreement between a broker and a borrower under the documented lending feature. [1]

The agreement records financial terms and requires the relevant authorization rather than merely publishing an informal promise. Identify the vault, broker, borrower and repayment parameters together. A ledger agreement can make obligations inspectable, but it does not guarantee repayment or replace an assessment of collateral, counterparty risk and applicable law. [1]

The LoanSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using LoanSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
